# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT B KS-923 PASS WITH FINDINGS (#869, tier 2)** — `313f96519` on `a821bd0aa` (2026-09-06 21:06→21:22 AEST, ~35 min; own mktemp clone; four tampered orchestrators written as SEPARATE files in scratch and graded via the suite's own hook, so **no tamper ever entered a repo working tree**) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It answered the builder's own question by falsifying its premise.** The builder said no behavioural discriminator exists between `bash "$p"` and a bare path when the file is executable; the gate found one — a shebang naming a nonexistent interpreter (bare path fails at `execve`, `bash` reads it as a comment) — and used it to show CELL 8 is **both false-quiet and false-loud**: a bare-path reversion with the literal left in a COMMENT keeps it green, a cosmetic brace change reds it, and its unique coverage over CELL 7 is zero. **F2 is the find of the pass:** `${ORCH_SH:-…}` treats set-but-empty as unset, so an empty value silently grades the SHIPPED file and prints a transcript **byte-identical (same sha256) to a genuine proof run** — a red-proof that can grade the wrong subject with nothing in the output to say so. **F1:** `[ ! -f ]` is true for a mode-000 file, so the fixed orchestrator gives byte-for-byte the PRE-FIX verdict one state over. It proved no fixture trips more than one condition by HASHING every file in all four, verified the healthy path byte-identical rather than via the suite, built its own gitleaks canary from RANDOM fabricated tokens (not a documented example pair, which gitleaks allowlists and which would have reported a false clean), and **publicly retracted a mid-session observation** after finding both its causes were its own instrument (a `head`-truncated listing read as complete, and a stub whose unescaped `$dir` its own shell expanded). |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s140d, seat B) | **KS-923 round 1 (PR #869)** — `a821bd0aa` → `313f96519` (a `require_job` guard on the security orchestrator's Stage 2, which had none; suite 9/9, red-proof 6/3 with three states proved separately and CELL 9 as a live control for the absence assertion) | 1 | **0.85** | 0.85 | **PASS WITH FINDINGS; a fix round after a pass, so the two-round cap is untouched.** Deductions: the guard tests existence rather than readability (F1 — the fixed defect one state over, in a shared helper), and its own harness could silently grade the shipped file (F2). **PROTECT: it named CELL 8 as the weakest part of its OWN work in the READY and asked for a judgement** — which is precisely what let the gate spend its time falsifying the premise instead of rediscovering the doubt. It also took only the stage-2 half of a sibling ticket, declared the overlap in three places, and reported that its first F2 fixture quietly covered half the ticket. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s141, seat A) | **KS-921 round 1 (PR #870, tier 1)** — a structural guard for the runtime re-link invariant, wired as preflight leg 13 so it blocks every push (suite 18/0/0; `run-shell-suites.sh` 14/14; full 13-leg preflight PASSED in the hook on the commit itself) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Gate not yet run — this row scores the BUILD and the honesty. **Both clauses red-proofed INDEPENDENTLY as required**: the real tree at `d602a1536` reds clause A on exactly nft-certificate/referral/staking with governance green and clause B silent; governance-minus-its-prune reds B alone with A green. Fixtures materialised with `git show`, never `checkout`, in a tree holding another branch. Clause B ships report-only as ruled, with a strict-mode exit

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
